Name: Enrique Cerdo.
Question: How do you know when it's time to ask a grown child to move out of your house?
Answer: I’m of mixed feelings about this one. On the one hand, I got “kicked out” at 17 and it was probably one of the best things that ever happened to me. I had to grow up, quit farting around and do something with my life. It would not have helped me if I could have stayed home with my parents. But! I tell my nieces and nephews all the time to stay home and sponge off mom and dad for as long as possible. By eldest niece lived with my sister and her husband until she was 27 and got married. She also has no student loan debt or other debt for that matter. As long as you all get along and them being there isn’t causing an issue, I say don’t worry about it too much. But if they aren’t making forward progress towards a degree or a career, or if they are causing problems for you or other residents, time for them to go.

Name: Enrique Cerdo.
Question: What are the advantages of sending your kid to government schools?
Answer: In the US at least, most government run schools are actually quite good. The vast majority of students attending ivy league schools and/or receiving advanced degrees attended government run schools. They are almost always better than Home Schooling and can often times compete with private schools, depending on the courses and programs your kid gets into. Keep in mind that the private schools can dump low performing and problematic students or refuse to admit students with cognitive or physical disabilities. Which tends to skew their numbers. Additionally, the government run schools foster a common experience with the kids that attend them and can also help develop social and interpersonal skills that often times do not develop in Homeschooling situations. MY personal opinion is that private schools should be much more heavily regulated. Especially the so called “Charter Schools”. And, homeschooling should be illegal.

Question: How can I maximize my time and see as much as possible on a short weekend trip to a new city?
Answer: The one piece of advice I can give you is not to go for a cheaper hotel outside of the area you want to be in. If it is a short trip, you don’t want to spend 1–2 hours on the train every day. Spend a bit extra and get a hotel right in the area near the things you want to go to.
